chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Ahmad ibn Hammad who said, Muhammad ibn Murazim informed me from his father or his uncle who said,

I witnessed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was accounting for a representative of his, and the representative was frequently saying, 'By Allah, I have not betrayed, by Allah, I have not betrayed.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'O this man, your betrayal and your wastage of my wealth are the same, because the evil of the betrayal is upon you.'

Then he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'If one of you were to flee from his sustenance, it would pursue him until it reaches him, just as if he were to flee from his death, it would pursue him until it reaches him.'
The one who betrays, a portion of his sustenance is deducted for him, and its burden is written against him.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of betrayal on a person's sustenance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual gravity of financial trustworthiness, where Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) equates betrayal with wastage, emphasizing that the primary burden of sin falls upon the trustee. It integrates a Prophetic saying linking the inevitability of death and sustenance to the concept of divine accounting, where misappropriation of wealth is recorded as a spiritual debt. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that material transactions are inextricably linked to one's eternal record and divine provision.
